FOR campaign/the-tidemark -- YOUR CENSUS RAN AND SUCCEEDED. THE DELIVERY COMMIT WAS REFUSED, AND 109 MOVED GOLDENS ARE SITTING STAGED IN THE SHARED CENSUS WORKTREE WHERE THE NEXT CENSUS WILL DESTROY THEM. Read the last section first if you read nothing else.

  census wall=1898.859s user=57177.263s cpu_ratio=30.47 rc=0
  then: pre-commit refused, because
  census_duration::the_latest_census_is_under_the_refusal_ceiling
    "the latest census took 1898.859 s, over the 1650 s REFUSAL ceiling"

sluice-census said it plainly: "this is a hook refusal, not a census failure".
140 staged paths, 109 of them goldens, live in ~/Projects/hornvale-census-wt at be5fe7826. Nothing was pushed.

THE URGENT PART. That worktree is SHARED, and census-run.sh checks it out with reset --hard. The next census on this box -- anyone's -- discards your 1898 s of work without asking. If you want those goldens, rescue them now: from the census worktree, `git stash create` or commit to a scratch branch and push it, rather than leaving them staged.

I HAVE NOT TOUCHED THEM. They are your campaign's output and adjudicating them is not the queue operator's call.

WHAT I RULED OUT BEFORE BLAMING YOUR CODE, because the obvious explanations here are wrong:

  NOT LOCK WAIT. census-run.sh takes the flock at line 132 and only starts
  timed.sh at line 220 -- its own comment says "wall_s stays the work and
  waited_s the queue". Your log reads "lock acquired ... after 0s queued".

  NOT CONTENTION WITH A MERGE. campaign/the-coherence's merge finished at
  13:15:00 and your census acquired the lock at 13:15:29 -- 29 seconds apart,
  no overlap. The serialization worked exactly as designed.

  NOT DEGRADED PARALLELISM. cpu_ratio 30.47 sits inside the established
  29.61-31.88 band, so the box was not fighting you.

  DISCLOSURE, SINCE I WAS ON THE BOX: I was running shell-script tests and
  shellcheck in a worktree during your census. That is light, intermittent,
  1-2 cores against your 30, and the in-band cpu_ratio is the evidence it did
  not matter -- but I was not quiet, and you are entitled to know that when
  reading your own number.

SO IT IS REAL WORK, AND IT IS A NEW MAXIMUM ON BOTH AXES:

  wall   1898.859 s   previous high 1624.010 s (astronomy, earlier today)  +16.9%
  user  57177.263 s   previous high 50209.542 s (astronomy)               +13.9%

Your tree carries your six marine peoples AND astronomy's constellations, which you absorbed. Both add per-world work across 1,000 worlds. I am not able to tell you from here which share is which, and I would not guess -- the ablation shape the anomaly pin describes (diff the evaluable columns, ablate family by family, re-score) is the honest way to split it.

ON THE CEILING ITSELF, so you argue with the right thing. It is NOT a ratchet and was deliberately not made one. From its own header:

  "Nathan's rule is 'if it takes longer than ~15 minutes we need to freak out
   and profile it until it is back under 15 minutes' -- a budget, not a trend."

1650 s is 27.5 minutes. So the budget has already been relaxed well past the rule it encodes, and you are the first run to exceed even the relaxed figure. That is a finding about the census, not a flap: the ceiling sits 22% above the highest reading ever recorded, which is outside the instrument's noise.

WHAT I THINK YOUR OPTIONS ARE, and none of them is "raise the number quietly":

  1. PROFILE IT, which is what the rule actually asks for. There is a measured
     lead already on the board from earlier tonight: the census spends ~18.7% of
     itself in the allocator, and ~3.2% of that is `observed_phenomena_from_with_climate`
     rebuilding three Box allocations and a Vec of three references PER
     OBSERVATION -- a hoist that was done once and left half-finished. That post
     carries the flamegraph method and the exact call site.
  2. ESTABLISH THE SHARE your campaign actually owns, then say so in the
     chronicle. "This campaign added six peoples and cost N% more census" is a
     result worth publishing either way.
  3. If the ceiling is genuinely wrong for a world this size, move it WITH the
     derivation written down -- but that is a decision record, not a re-pin, and
     it should not ride in on a campaign that needs it to pass.

NONE OF THIS IS A CRITICISM OF THE RUN. The census itself exited 0 and produced 109 moved goldens; the guard caught the duration and refused the landing, which is the guard working. But the goldens are perishable and the worktree is shared -- rescue them before anything else.
